 : JUDGMENT :
The petitioners have filed this petition being aggrieved by the arbitral award passed by the Special Deputy Commissioner/Arbitrator, Bengaluru Urban A.P. No.28/2022 District, Bengaluru, in No.
LAQ / ARB / NH-7 / CR / 91 / 92 / 2011-12, 189 / 130 / 53 / 2012-13, 21 / 22 / 23 / 7 / 2014-15 dated 03.11.2020, which is amended subsequently on 18.12.2020 and 22.12.2020 in respect of Sy.
No.42 measuring 350 Sq. Meters i.e., 0-03459 guntas of Sonnappanahalli village, Jala Hobli,
Bengaluru North Addl. Taluka, Bengaluru Urban District.
.2.

The definite case of the petitioners is that the property bearing Sy. No.42 measuring 350 Sq.
Meters i.e., 0-03459 guntas of Sonnappanahalli village, Jala Hobli, Bengaluru North Addl. Taluka,
Bengaluru Urban District has been acquired under Preliminary Notification dated 09.12.2009 and Final Notification dated 30.07.2010
Subsequently the respondent No.2/LAO has awarded a total sum of Rs.25,22,566/- to the land and Rs. 11,200/- towards 52 Eucalyptus Trees belongs to the petitioners.

The petitioners received the same under protest and filed an application for enhancing the compensation at the rate of Rs.10,000/-
A.P. No.28/2022 per Sq. feet as on 15.05.2012.
Accordingly, the said application taken by the respondent No. 3 for consideration.
.3. In the said petition, the respondent No.2 filed statement of objection stating that the contention urged by the petitioners are baseless and the same are made without any substance.

The petitioners have not produced any relevant documents to justify their claim for enhanced compensation and the Shekar S C vs The Special Deputy Commissioner And ... on 9 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57153694/
2 claim of the petitioners cannot be sustained in law.

entities.text: Shekar S C vs The Special Deputy Commissioner
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, question of enhancement of compensation will not arise and the claim of the petitioners is liable to be dismissed by the respondent No.2.

Accordingly, prayed to dismiss the reference.
.4.

Thereafter, the Arbitrator hold an inquiry and passed common order in LAQ / ARB / NH-7 / CR / 91 9 /2011-12, 189/130/53/2012-13, 21/22/23/7/2014- 15 dated 03.11.2020, which is amended subsequently on 18.12.2020 and 22.12.2020.

Being aggrieved by the impugned Arbitral Award, the petitioners filed this petition under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, setting up the following :
:GROUNDS:
The petitioners claim that the the amount fixed by the respondent No. 2 was unfair and the respondent No. 1 while enhancing the compensation have not taken into consideration about the market value and other necessary facts to determine the fair compensation.
The award passed by the respondent No. 2 by fixing Rs. 1,314/- per Sq. feet is unjust and against to the provisions of New Act 2013.
The respondent No. 1 has not adopted the yardstick applied to the facts an circumstance of the case.

Among other grounds prayed to reconsider the impugned award and also alternative prayer to remand the matter to the Arbitrator for fresh consideration.
A.P. No.28/2022 .6.
The respondent No.2 and 3 have filed detailed objections claiming that the application is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
The petitioners had not filed any necessary documents in support of their claim as urged in the ground under reply.
The impugned award is not perverse and this petition is liable to be dismissed on this ground only.

The respondents 2 and 3 totally denied all the grounds claimed by the petitioners in the petition and among other grounds,
prayed for dismissal of the petition.
.7. The respondent No.1 did not appear before the Court and hence, the respondent No. 1 has been placed exparte.
The respondents 2 and 3 appeared before the Court through their Advocates.

The entire records in LAQ / ARB / NH-7 / CR / 91 /92/2011-12, 189/130/53/2012-13, 21/22/23/7/2014-15 dated 03.11.2020, which is amended subsequently on 18.12.2020 and 22.12.2020 secured from the Arbitrator.

On the basis of above, the points for consideration are as under:
1) Whether the impugned award of the Arbitrator/SLAO is against law, fact, evidence and probabilities of the case and liable to be intervened by this Court?
2) What order or award?

sentences.text: Heard the arguments.

Perused the materials on record, on that basis my findings on the above points are as under:
Points No.1 : In the negative Point No.2: As per final order, for the following:
REASONS .10. POINT NO.1:
Before proceeding further in this case, it is relevant to note an admitted and undisputed facts in this case.

The petitioners are the owner of the property bearing Sy. No.42 measuring 350 Sq. Meters i.e., 0-03459 guntas of Sonnappanahalli village, Jala Hobli, Bengaluru North Addl. Taluka, Bengaluru Urban District and the said property has been acquired for A.P. No.28/2022 widening of NH-7 under Preliminary Notification dated 09.12.2009 and Final Notification dated 30.07.2010
, is an admitted fact.

.11. It is also an admitted and undisputed fact in this case that the respondent No.2/Special Land Acquisition and Competent Authority of National Highways Authority of India being a SLAO determined the compensation at Rs.1,314/- per Sq. feet for the acquired land.

entities.text: Special Land Acquisition and Competent Authority of National Highways Authority of India
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: It is also admitted and undisputed fact that a sum of Rs.1,25,89,703/- after deducting of TDS of Rs. 13,98,856/- being the land value was disbursed to the petitioners as compensation.

The petitioners received the same under protest and filed an application for enhancing the compensation at the rate of Rs.10,000/-
per Sq. feet as on 15.05.2012.
Accordingly, the said application taken by the respondent No. 3 for consideration.

.12. Subsequent to the receipt of compensation or passing of the award, the petitioners filed an application before the respondent No.3 claiming that A.P. No.28/2022 they are entitled for compensation at the rate of Rs.10,000/- per Sq. feet as on 15.05.2012.

On basis of the said application, the respondent No.3 hold an inquiry and passed common order in LAQ / ARB / NH-7 /
CR / 91 /92/2011-12, 189/130/53/2012-13, 21/22/23/7/2014-15 dated 03.11.2020, which is amended subsequently on 18.12.2020 and 22.12.2020.

The respondent No.3 in its order enhanced the compensation at Rs.12,973/- per Sq. meter from Rs. 7,207/- per Sq. meter and awarded additional compensation of Rs.5,766/- per Sq. meter.
.13.
The said enhancement has been challenged by the petitioners in this petition.

The grievance of the petitioners is that the respondent No.1 ought to have enhanced the compensation @ Rs.
10,000/- per Sq. feet and these petitioners claim the same in the representation made to the respondent No.1.

Further claim of the petitioners is that the market value of the acquired property is more that Rs. 10,000/- per Sq. feet and they are entitled for compensation @ Rs. 15,000/-
A.P. No.28/2022 per Sq. feet and also claimed that the petitioners sought for fixation of the market value of the acquired property not less than Rs.15,000/- per Sq. feet.
Inspite of the specific made by the petitioners the respondent No.1 only fixed the market value at Rs. 2,625/- per Sq. feet.

In view of the aforesaid claim of the petitioners, it is for the petitioners to show that their acquired property fetches more value than Rs. 2,625/- per Sq. feet and the market value of the acquired property as on the date of preliminary notification is more than Rs. 10,000/- per Sq. feet.
After filing of this petition, this Court obtained the entire records from respondent No.1.

The said records nowhere Shekar S C vs The Special Deputy Commissioner And ... on 9 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57153694/
4 discloses that these petitioners have placed any material before the respondent No.1/ Arbitrator which substantiate the claim of petitioners that their property is valued more than Rs. 10,000/- per Sq. feet.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also not the case of the petitioners that the Arbitrator / respondent No.1 has fixed more value to the adjacent property of the petitioners or the other acquired property under the same notification.

When A.P. No.28/2022 the petitioners have failed to place any material before the respondent No.1 to show that their property was worth more than Rs.10,000/- per Sq. feet, certainly the respondent No.1 cannot accept their claim.

Even before this Court, the petitioners have not placed any material to show that the respondent No.1 has awarded more compensation to the similarly acquired property or there is no material even on this date before this court to show that the acquired property or the adjacent property values more than Rs. 10,000/- per Sq. feet.
Therefore, viewed from any angle, the petitioners have failed to make out any grounds or placed any material to intervene with the award passed by the respondent No.1 and accept their claim.

Accordingly, the point No.1 is held in the negative.
.19. Point No.2:
In view of my above finding, I proceed to pass the following.

A.P. No.28/2022 ORDER Petition filed under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act,
1996 is hereby dismissed.

Consequently, the impugned award passed by the respondent No.1 in case LAQ / ARB / NH-7 / CR /
91 / 92 / 2011-12, 189/130/53/2012-13, 21/22/23/7/2014- 15 dated 03.11.2020 which is amended subsequently on 18.12.2020 and 22.12.2020 in respect of Sy. No.42 measuring 350 Sq. Meters i.e.,
0-03459 guntas of Hunsamarannahalli village, Jala Hobli, Bengaluru North Addl. Taluka,
Bengaluru Urban District is hereby confirmed.
Office is directed to send back the Lower Court Records.

pronounced in open Court on this the 9th day of September, 2024) (PADMA PRASAD) II Addl. City Civil and Sessions Judge, & Spl. Judge, Bangalore.
